method: git-tracked non-test source read from git archive at the recorded commits; one sample per rule (seed 20261101-<rule>, at most 15); one rater (the author) labelled every sampled hit explicitly. Informal: single rater, small samples. tp means a reviewer would agree the site could produce the rule's wrong behavior (torn record, duplicate effect after a reported failure, give-up on a transient failure) under a reachable condition.

status.failure_after_effect: cut: precision 0.00 (0 tp of 1 hit), below 0.7 (n=1; small sample, informal single rater)

contamination: All four rules (two since cut) were designed after reading the hard-benchmark defects H01, H07 and H08 (evals/hard/private/oracles.json), so their recall on those cases is not evidence: two_write_append fires at H07 store.rs:1189 (window 1180-1191, agent-rally-point 25fc7e5); failure_after_effect fires at H08 lib.rs:1769 (window 1765-1780, babc9b0); sibling_retryable fires at H01 scan-lock.ts:458 (window 457-459, NavGator 3723d05); timeout_terminal does not fire on H01 363-367 because that branch returns ok:false without a status or retryable field.

cut_rules_informal.two_write_append on Python file handles: not built: buffered text files usually flush a short record and its newline in one write
cut_rules_informal.sibling_retryable without a catch-all gu: any function mixing retryable true/false fired; 0/3 on NavGator scan-lock.ts after the fix (each false return was a distinct operational error)
